# Merging the Last Two Commits in Git

You can combine (squash) the last two commits into one using **interactive rebase**:

## Method 1: Interactive Rebase (Most Common)

```bash
git rebase -i HEAD~2
```

This opens an editor showing your last 2 commits:

```
pick abc1234 First commit message
pick def5678 Second commit message
```

Change the **second** line from `pick` to `squash` (or `s`):

```
pick abc1234 First commit message
squash def5678 Second commit message
```

- **Save and close** the editor.
- A new editor opens to **combine/edit the commit message**.
- Save again, and you're done!

---

## Method 2: Soft Reset (Quick Alternative)

```bash
git reset --soft HEAD~2
git commit -m "New combined commit message"
```

This moves the branch pointer back 2 commits while keeping all changes staged, then creates a single new commit.

---

## Key Notes

| Option | Meaning |
|------------|----------------------------------------------|
| `pick` | Keep the commit as-is |
| `squash` | Merge into the previous commit (combine messages) |
| `fixup` | Merge into the previous commit (discard this message) |

> ⚠️ **Warning**: Both methods **rewrite history**. If you've already pushed these commits, you'll need to force push:
> ```bash
> git push --force
> ```
> Avoid this on **shared branches** unless your team agrees.
